title: 2026-11-04_Okiru_Worm_Investigation_2b1
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from the internal network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the Okiru worm, a variant of the Mirai botnet malware. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the worm's behavior, and contain the threat.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux commands and system administration.
Familiarity with network security concepts and incident response procedures.
outcomes: Enumerate running services and identify suspicious activities.
Investigate network communication and determine the command and control (C2) infrastructure.
Analyze persistence mechanisms and contain the threat.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual CPU-intensive and network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Access the entry host:
```bash
ssh cyrano@patient-zero
```

2. List all running services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

3. Identify suspicious services:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

4. Check service details:
```bash
systemctl status <service_name>
```

5. Identify the suspicious service:
The service responsible for the suspicious activity is `sysnet-monitor.service`. This is the final flag.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Access the entry host:
```bash
ssh cyrano@patient-zero
```

2. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl cat sysnet-monitor.service
```

3. Identify the port number:
Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file. The port number is specified in this line.

4. Verify the port:
```bash
ss -tulnp | grep <port_number>
```

5. Identify the port number:
The port number responsible for the suspicious activity is `52869`. This is the final flag.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the beaconing service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Access the entry host:
```bash
ssh cyrano@patient-zero
```

2. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```

3. Identify the suspicious timer:
Look for timers associated with the `sysnet-monitor.service`.

4. Inspect the timer details:
```bash
systemctl cat sysnet-monitor.timer
```

5. Identify the timer name:
The timer responsible for the suspicious activity is `sysnet-monitor.timer`. This is the final flag.
